reason: The text describes God's miraculous plagues delivered through Moses against Pharaoh and Egypt. While the Egyptian magicians (the elite intellectual class) fail to replicate certain plagues and Pharaoh stubbornly resists despite devastating divine judgments, the narrative does not portray regular people as being smarter than the elite. Rather, it illustrates the power of God's will and the hardening of Pharaoh's heart. The text contains no comparison suggesting the wisdom or intelligence of common people exceeds that of the elite; the magicians' failure is attributed to divine power, not to superior intelligence of common Egyptians.
